edges.description: The germline variant is the first hit. The genetics series predicts that every tumour also needs a second, somatic DICER1 hit, and proposes that it takes place in the embryonic pituitary.
In these tumours the RNase IIIb hotspot mutations cause improper processing of microRNA precursors, with aberrant 5p-derived products and mature microRNAs skewed from 5p towards 3p.

How the microRNA imbalance produces the embryonic-appearing tumour is not established; the genetics series leaves the mechanism to be explored, and the molecular study names the pathways that are dysregulated.

edges.description: The tumour's ACTH drives the hypercortisolism: ACTH was raised in nine of the ten children with Cushing syndrome.
A large suprasellar mass invading the cavernous sinus, in a child with progressive ophthalmoplegia.
The mass may encompass the optic chiasm; no cited source measures the compression against the reduced visual acuity.
The genetics series names local effects of the tumour causing raised intracranial pressure as one possible cause of the infants' deaths. No cited source shows the mechanism.

nodes.description: The tumour itself: arrested pituitary development with uncontrolled proliferation, in a lesion composed of Rathke-type epithelium, folliculostellate cells, small primitive cells and secretory cells. evidence.snippet: Pathologically, the tumors exhibit arrested pituitary development and uncontrolled proliferation and are composed of Rathke epithelium, folliculostellate cells, small primitive cells, and secretory cells with ACTH or, less often, growth hormone (GH) immunoexpression

evidence.reference_title: Pituitary blastoma.
evidence.snippet: Ultrastructurally, the tissue resembled fetal pituitary of 10-12 weeks gestation and contained fully differentiated corticotrophs and somatotrophs, scant cells of glycoprotein-hormone producing type with small secretory granules, and glandular epithelial cells consistent with committed, but largely undifferentiated Rathke-type epithelium.

nodes.description: The commonest presentation, in 10 of the 17 children of the outcome series. In nine of them ACTH was raised at diagnosis, so their hypercortisolism is ACTH-dependent; in the tenth a raised random serum cortisol was recorded. Seven children had no cushingoid signs at diagnosis, two of them with a raised ACTH.

evidence.snippet: Pituitary blastoma is a rare tumor of the anterior pituitary that generally occurs in children aged 2 years and younger and presents with Cushing syndrome, ophthalmoplegia, and/or diabetes insipidus.

evidence.reference_title: Pituitary blastoma: a pathognomonic feature of germ-line DICER1 mutations.

nodes.description: The DICER1 defect skews the tumour's microRNAs from the 5p to the 3p arm and dysregulates hundreds of microRNAs and their messenger RNA targets; PRAME is the most upregulated gene.

nodes.description: Given after surgery to two of the 17 children of the outcome series, one for persistent residual disease and one for progression. Both later had a vascular complication, moyamoya disease or an aneurysm, though the authors note the aneurysm may also have been associated with earlier surgery; the series advises that radiotherapy for this tumour be considered with special caution.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline DICER1 variant, most often one predicted to inactivate the allele, is found in most children tested: 9 of 10 in the genetics series, 12 of 13 in the outcome series and 11 of 14 in a 2022 review. In the genetics series it was known to be inherited in five children and de novo in two. On its own it is thought not to produce the tumour: the genetics series predicts a second, somatic hit in every case.

evidence.snippet: Lymphocyte or saliva DNA samples ascertained from ten infants with PitB were screened and nine were found to harbor a heterozygous germ-line DICER1 mutation.

nodes.description: The tumour as a mass: typically an enhancing sellar mass, with or without cysts or cavernous sinus involvement, a median 3 cm across. Its extension into the cavernous sinuses and around the optic chiasm is the likely source of the cranial nerve palsies and the reduced visual acuity; the genetics series names local effects of the tumour causing raised intracranial pressure as one possible cause of the infants' deaths. No cited source measures either step.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Outcomes and Complications of Pituitary Blastoma.
evidence.snippet: Radiographically, an enhancing sellar mass, with or without intratumoral cysts and cavernous sinus involvement, was typically seen on magnetic resonance imaging, with a median greatest diameter of 3 cm (range, 1.7-12 cm) ... enhancement was not seen in one patient.

nodes.description: The transforming event: a somatic hit on the remaining DICER1 allele in the tumour, usually a missense mutation at a metal ion-binding residue of the RNase IIIb domain, and in a minority loss of the wild-type allele. In the genetics series eight of the nine tumour changes found were confirmed to be somatic.

evidence.snippet: DICER1 alterations were identified in 13 of 14 tumor samples tested (hotspot mutations, n = 11; loss of heterozygosity, n = 2).

nodes.description: The first treatment in every child of the outcome series, in four of them in stages: gross or near-total resection in 7, subtotal resection in 9 and biopsy alone in 1. The extent of resection was the one treatment factor associated with survival, and surgery was the only treatment in five of the nine survivors.
